content:
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are scheduled to be unveiled next month, featuring the all-new A20 Pro chip; this weekend, a reputable tipster shared the expected performance gains based on supply chain information.

A20 Pro chip is expected to deliver an 18% performance boost along with 30% greater power efficiency

Apple will introduce its latest chip technology breakthrough — the A20 Pro — at its big September event.

The A20 Pro will be Apple's first chip manufactured using TSMC's 2nm process. It is also rumored to adopt the new Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module (WMCM) packaging technology.

Based on all these innovations, we've been expecting a larger-than-usual performance leap for this year's chip.

Weibo tipster "Fixed Focus Digital" posted this weekend, sharing the following upgrades for the A20 Pro over the A19 Pro based on supply chain information:

  • 18% performance improvement
  • 30% power efficiency improvement

Details will undoubtedly be more granular when Apple officially announces them next month. Apple typically breaks out the gains separately for the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine.

But if these numbers hold true, it would be a rather impressive leap. Greater power efficiency means better battery life while still delivering the most powerful performance ever.

Combined with the speed improvements in iOS 27 itself, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are shaping up to be an exciting upgrade in terms of performance.

What are your thoughts on the rumored performance gains for the A20 Pro? Share your opinions in the comments section.
